title: A bridge between two books
offscreen: The same challenge works with other materials: straws and tape, two chairs and some string.

materials.label: Two books of the same height
Scissors and a little sticky tape

steps.text: Put the two books on the table, a hand's span apart.
With just one sheet build a bridge from one book to the other: you can fold it, roll it, cut it.
Place one coin at a time in the middle of the bridge, gently.
If it gives way, look at where it gave way, change one thing and try again.

levels.control: The bridge itself: it holds or it gives way, and you can see where. Nobody needs to say if it's right.
levels.observe: What changes from one try to the next, and whether they say it before trying.

intro.bo: {nome}, today we really build something. You need two books, a sheet of paper and a few coins.
intro.pilu: {nome}, a paper bridge can hold more than you think. You only find out by trying.
intro.tango: {nome}! A bridge! If it falls down, it tells you where to make it stronger. Someone told me.

outro.bo: You tried and changed things, {nome}. The books go back on the shelf, the coins in the jar.
outro.pilu: Every bridge that gave way told you something, {nome}. Now let's put everything away.
outro.tango: What bridges! {nome}, shall we tidy up? I'll count the coins. One, two... lots.
